title: Crucible Violation Row
description: One JSON object per line of violations.jsonl. This is a deliberately denormalised long-format table: one row per (record, finding). It exists so that 'which mistakes does the generator make repeatedly' can be answered with a group-by, across many runs, without reopening a single verdict record. Every row MUST be traceable back to a verdict via record_id.

taxonomy_version.description: Semver of the violation taxonomy in force when this row was written. Rows carrying different taxonomy versions may not be compared without an explicit mapping.

level.description: How bad. Deliberately separate from the code, so that severity can be re-tuned without invalidating historical rows.

json_pointer.description: RFC 6901 pointer into the proposal object identifying the offending field.

fingerprint.description: sha256 over the canonicalised triple (code, json_pointer, normalized observed value). Stable across runs for the same finding, so 'new vs unchanged vs resolved' is answerable.

unverifiable.description: True when this row records an inability to check rather than a detected defect. Rows with unverifiable=true MUST be excluded from any 'error rate' statistic.

detector.description: Which component raised the finding, as name@semver.
